title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stock in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll be linking a detailed spreadsheet that tracks the breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week

    . This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Overall: Positive

The major indices continue to trade constructively, holding well above their rising 10- and 20-day moving averages, with no signs of technical deterioration or broad selling pressure. The trend of higher highs and higher lows remains intact, signaling healthy momentum and strong underlying demand. While the indices hover around their 50-day moving averages, this zone may bring some short-term volatility, which is typical and not yet concerning.

A mild pullback over the next week or two would be a constructive development, allowing overextended stocks to consolidate and form new bases. Internals remain supportive, with breadth and momentum readings still positive. That said, sector rotation continues to play out under the surface, with leadership shifting and new groups emerging—an important dynamic for traders to monitor closely.

Importantly, earnings season is still in force. Traders should remain mindful of upcoming earnings dates before initiating any new positions, as earnings volatility can introduce additional risk. However, this period also presents opportunity: earnings gaps and episodic pivots remain valid and actionable strategies when backed by strong volume and favorable setups. Overall, while a pause or pullback wouldn’t be unwelcome, the market’s current structure remains bullish and supportive of selective, well-managed long exposure.

Risk Management and Exposure Control

  • Maintain a Cautiously Bullish Stance:
    The trend remains constructive with major indices holding above rising 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages. However, with momentum showing signs of slowing, continue to maintain a positive bias while remaining agile in case of a pullback.

  • Scale Exposure Selectively:
    Gradually increase exposure only in confirmed high-quality setups. Avoid adding aggressively until strength resumes, especially in leading sectors.

  • Actively Manage Underperformers:
    Reduce or exit trades that lose relative strength or fail at key resistance. Reallocate into technically sound names showing clear trend continuation.

Market Monitoring and Internal Indicators

  • Track Index Behavior and Trend Continuity:
    Higher lows and steepening moving averages suggest healthy price structure. Watch how small caps behave near the 50-day and whether large/mid caps continue to hold support.

  • Watch for Internal Deceleration:
    Breadth and momentum remain positive, but recent narrowing (e.g., a 1:1 high/low ratio) indicates possible digestion. Use this as a cue to prepare for slower follow-through and more selective participation.

  • Monitor for Early Warning Signs:
    A breakdown in internal strength without price confirmation (e.g., divergence) may signal risk ahead. Use sector breadth and relative strength screens to validate setups.

Sector and Theme Development

  • Monitor Growth Sector Follow-Through:
    Technology, Consumer Discretionary, and Semiconductors are key watch areas. Tech has slipped in rank but may resume leadership. Look for stabilization and rotation back into growth.

  • Assess Sector Rotation:
    Defensive sectors like Utilities and Consumer Staples are sliding in rank, while Energy and Healthcare are rolling over at resistance. Monitor Industrials and Financials for rotation potential.

  • Identify Emerging Themes:
    Focus on under-the-radar groups building new bases. Favor stocks with improving RS lines, higher lows, and constructive volume.

Capital Allocation and Trade Execution

  • Stick to High-Quality Setups:
    Prioritize trades with:

    • Well-defined technical bases or flags

    • Breakouts with confirming volume

    • Pullbacks to rising 10-/20-day MAs

  • Keep Risk Parameters Tight:
    Use stops below logical support zones. Maintain moderate position sizes and avoid concentration in any one sector, especially those under distribution.

  • Stay Liquid and Avoid Overexposure:
    Given potential short-term chop, maintain enough cash to pivot quickly. Don’t feel pressure to be fully allocated in a rotating environment.

Daily Reassessment and Strategy Adaptation

  • Support Retests Are Likely:
    Be prepared for a retest of the rising 10-/20-day MAs. A successful defense would affirm strength; failure may signal a broader correction.

  • Adapt Based on Internal Conditions:

    • If internals expand and indices reclaim leadership: Increase exposure gradually into top technical setups.

    • If internals weaken or indices stall at resistance: Trim exposure and increase cash defensively.

  • Let Setup Expansion Drive Action:
    Avoid focusing solely on index movement. Follow the number and quality of actionable setups—this is often a more accurate gauge of underlying market strength.

Key Focus Areas

  • Patience on Entry Timing:
    Wait for clear signals. Don’t chase extended breakouts—focus on entries near support with clear risk levels.

  • Track Leadership Rotation:
    Keep a close eye on sectors rotating into strength. Emerging leadership from growth sectors would justify increasing conviction.

  • Flexibility is Essential:
    Be willing to shift positioning quickly. A rotational or volatile environment requires responsiveness and discipline.

Bottom Line:

The market remains in a healthy, uptrending structure, but recent internal deceleration suggests the next phase may be rotational or corrective. Stay focused on high-quality names, manage risk tightly, and allow setups—not index moves alone—to dictate engagement. Remain bullish but measured, ready to increase exposure on confirmation or defend capital on deterioration.
